outcome: Delayed wound healing (>1 month from episiotomy, vaginal tear, or C-section)
cohort: The study included 743 pregnant individuals with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) from a multicenter registry (PIANO) who provided postpartum wound healing data.
finding: Immunomodulator use was significantly associated with delayed episiotomy wound healing, whereas no such association was found for vaginal tears or C-section wound healing with any IBD therapy.
mod_finding: C-section deliveries, which occurred at high rates especially in Crohn's disease patients, showed no reported delays in postpartum wound healing, while episiotomies were common and associated with delayed healing in those using immunomodulators.
